description.value: The study examined whether individual differences in self-reported self-control are associated with successful emotion regulation and its neural correlates, including amygdala activity and amygdala-prefrontal functional connectivity.

spans.text: Here, we tested whether high self-reported self-control is related to successful emotion regulation on the behavioral and neural level.

value: We expected that high self-controllers would show greater success in emotion regulation, indicated by fewer negative emotions and stronger amygdala down-regulation.
Furthermore, we expected regulation success in high self-controllers to be related to increased recruitment of prefrontal regions and/or to stronger PFC-amygdala functional connectivity.

value: The whole-brain analysis of the RegulateNeg > WatchNeg contrast showed increased activation in lateral parts of the PFC, medial areas such as the midcingulate cortex and superior medial gyrus, and the inferior parietal lobe; together these areas represent the regulation network.

spans.text: As expected, the whole-brain analysis of the RegulateNeg > WatchNeg contrast showed increased activation in lateral parts of the PFC, such as the left and right middle (MFG), inferior (IFG) and superior frontal gyrus ( P < 0.05, FWE-corrected; Figure 3a ). Similarly, medial areas like the midcingulate cortex and superior medial gyrus were activated, as well as the IPL. Together these areas represent the regulation-network ( Supplementary Table S5 ).

value: Within the amygdala ROIs, there was increased activity during WatchNeg > RegulateNeg in the right and left amygdala, indicating neural down-regulation during emotion regulation. The extracted betas showed the same pattern as the subjective ratings, with amygdala activity lowest in WatchNeu, highest in WatchNeg, and medium in RegulateNeg trials.

spans.text: Within the amygdala ROIs, there was increased activity during WatchNeg > RegulateNeg (i.e. the neural down-regulation effect when looked at inversely) in the right ( t max = 4.86, k = 41, MNI peak coordinates (PCs) = 27 −1 −20) and left amygdala ( t max = 4.15, k = 25, MNI PCs = −24 −4 −20) at P < 0.05, FWE-SVC ( Figure 3b (I) ). The extracted betas of the activated cluster showed the same pattern as the subjective rating, with amygdala activity lowest in WatchNeu-, highest in WatchNeg-, and medium in RegulateNeg-trials ( Figure 3b (II) ).

value: Trait self-control was related to higher functional connectivity during RegulateNeg > WatchNeg between the left amygdala and lateral and medial prefrontal areas, including the middle frontal gyrus, inferior frontal gyrus, and anterior cingulate cortex, as well as the insula. Higher overall left amygdala functional connectivity was associated with lower intensity of negative feelings, indicating greater emotion-regulation success.
